HYPOTHETICAL UNITED NATIONS EXAMPLE — Committee meeting record

The representative proposed that participating States submit a voluntary progress update by 30 June each year. Several delegations requested further consultations. The Chair noted that no decision on the proposed timetable had been adopted and that consideration would continue at the next session.
question: Did the committee adopt the proposed annual reporting deadline of 30 June?
answer: No. The Chair noted that no decision on the proposed timetable had been adopted and that consideration would continue at the next session.

HYPOTHETICAL UNITED NATIONS EXAMPLE — Programme update

The Secretariat reported voluntary contributions of USD 2.4 million during the first half of the reporting year. Of this amount, USD 600,000 was earmarked for training activities. These figures exclude pledges that had not yet been received.
question: How much of the received voluntary contributions was earmarked for training activities?
answer: USD 600,000 was earmarked for training activities.

HYPOTHETICAL UNITED NATIONS EXAMPLE — Consultation summary

The regional consultations were open to government representatives, accredited civil society organisations and invited technical experts. Participants could submit written observations in advance. The summary records the views expressed and does not constitute an agreed intergovernmental outcome.
question: Who could participate in the regional consultations, and does the summary constitute an agreed intergovernmental outcome?
answer: Government representatives, accredited civil society organisations and invited technical experts could participate.
